title: Transferred two-cell readouts retained 55 to 59 percent median sensitivity in two passive adult worm circuit models
abstract: We tested whether a remote two-cell readout selected from one adult worm electrical map transfers to the other map. The passive model used contact counts as symmetric conductances, mean weighted degree one, leak 0.1 and equal independent Gaussian current noise. We tested 133 common sources in each direction. Full transfer of cell choice and weights retained median sensitivities of 0.5866 and 0.5465 relative to the best test pair. Refitting weights on the selected cells raised the medians to 0.7721 and 0.7316. Full retention was below half for 60 and 59 sources. An exact per-source split separated placement and weight losses. Independent calculations agreed within 3.68e-13; removing one tied optimum left the main result unchanged. A post-plan audit found lower retention when selected direct training links were absent from the test table. Partial electrical annotation prevents separating real animal variation from missing reconstruction. All 24 model settings are reported. Two maps, assumed conductances, exact noise knowledge and no measured activity limit biological claims. Original code, aggregate evidence, figures, hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External record-level data are excluded.

display.caption: Placement and weight transfer in two passive adult worm maps. Each direction tests 133 known source identities. Full retention divides the fixed training readout sensitivity by the best test-pair sensitivity.
